Synthetic test speech record

Model and runtime
-----------------

Model: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice (Apache-2.0)
https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice

GGUF Q8_0 weights (Apache-2.0):
https://huggingface.co/Serveurperso/Qwen3-TTS-GGUF

- Talker: qwen-talker-1.7b-customvoice-Q8_0.gguf
  SHA-256: cab2cff67a0a557310febe558dc83076b28ed790e491867eb2751759f4cd89fa
- Codec: qwen-tokenizer-12hz-Q8_0.gguf
  SHA-256: 1883beeed99348fc35e23dd225e9082f93f6f8c109330a33d935baa8acdbfd94

Runtime: qwentts.cpp with ggml (both MIT), using the CUDA backend.
Voice: built-in speaker Aiden. The synthesis used this built-in voice
without a reference audio input.
Settings: language="en", voice="Aiden", greedy decoding without sampling,
seed 7. Two synthesis runs with these settings produced identical bytes.

Spoken text
-----------

Every morning the small boat leaves the harbor before sunrise. The crew
checks the nets, counts the floats, and writes the weather in a notebook.
By noon they return with fresh fish for the market.

Processing and conversion
-------------------------

The float32 synthesis output was converted to 16-bit samples with
round(clip(x, -1, 1) * 32767). No volume normalization, silence trimming,
or noise removal was applied. The source WAV is 24 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM,
11.68 seconds long:
SHA-256: 5b99d9424e03c56e358101e03fd82e442fc0fa42d39df5b1db6e48b7966f60ab

The full utterance was resampled to 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit little-endian
(s16le) PCM WAVE using FFmpeg 8.0.1-3ubuntu2, libswresample 6.1.100:

ffmpeg -y -hide_banner -loglevel error -i fixture-small-boat.wav \
  -map_metadata -1 -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le \
  -fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact -f wav \
  small_boat_16khz_mono_s16le.wav

The resulting asset contains 186,880 samples, 11.68 seconds, with a 44-byte WAVE header
(373,804 bytes in total):
SHA-256: f80e9a97d1294af40e1f6076454437825388d4ceff87542abd1127bf1ae587bb

tests/fixtures/generate_synthetic_speech.sh verifies the source WAV
checksums and reproduces this conversion from the repository root.

License

This generated audio is distributed under the MIT license as part of
listenflow-faster-whisper, together with its code. The synthesis model
and GGUF weights retain their Apache-2.0 license as external synthesis
inputs. The distribution contains the generated speech and this record.

Reuse in listenflow-fastest-whisper
----------------------------------

Copied from repository sync-dev-org/listenflow-faster-whisper at commit
d7c6087edd7b871bebda8d245a71a5f22b01cdc3:
- tests/fixtures/small_boat_16khz_mono_s16le.wav
- tests/fixtures/small_boat_speech_record.txt
- tests/fixtures/generate_synthetic_speech.sh

listenflow-fastest-whisper also distributes the copied synthetic audio,
this record, and the conversion script under MIT.

The conversion script in this repository accepts only the small-boat
24 kHz source WAV. The related repository's script also converted a separate
warmup recording into its package; that conversion is omitted here.
From this repository's root, reproduce the fixture with:

bash tests/fixtures/generate_synthetic_speech.sh fixture-small-boat.wav

The script checks the source WAV SHA-256 and retains the original FFmpeg
bit-exact conversion options. The original 24 kHz WAV is an external input
and is not included in this repository.
